problem: Express $2\cos^{2}\left(\frac{5\pi }{3}\right)-1$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
solution:
Use the alternative cosine double-angle formula:

$$
2\cos^2 x-1=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute $x=\frac{5\pi}{3}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2\cos^2\left(\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)-1&=\cos\left(2\cdot \frac{5\pi}{3}\right)\\&=\cos\left(\frac{10\pi}{3}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

problem: Express $5-10\sin^{2}{20}^{\circ}$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
solution:
Factor out $5$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&5-10\sin^2\left(20^\circ\right)\\&\qquad=5\left(1-2\sin^2\left(20^\circ\right)\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Use the alternative cosine double-angle formula:

$$
1-2\sin^2 x=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute $x=20^\circ$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
1-2\sin^2\left(20^\circ\right)&=\cos\left(2\cdot 20^\circ\right)\\&=\cos\left(40^\circ\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Keep the outside factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}
5\left(1-2\sin^2\left(20^\circ\right)\right)&=5\cos\left(40^\circ\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
